rungs.title: Divisor–Chern identity as an exact equality on the pinned cycle class: the class of a Cartier divisor D equals the rational image of c₁(𝒪(D)), sign determined
rungs.note: Checked at this repository's pin in the port (2026-11-24). Statement (upstream's HasDivisorClassOfCartierData, as defined at the pin): for every invertible sheaf L, unit extension E with L^an ≅ its section sheaf, and Cartier datum c representing L, sheafCycleClassOnCycles 1 c.divisor = integralToRationalCohomology 2 E.firstChernClass, with sign +. sheafCycleClassOnCycles is upstream main's (Other/AlgebraicGeometry/Cycle/SheafClass.lean), built from main's cycleComponentSheafClass, the class of record; no copy is staged. Exactness on main's class comes from the port's bridge cycleComponentSheafClass_eq_injectiveModel (no scalar) and the transport of the normalization (componentTransport). Signs met on the way are in docs/conventions.md (orientation against winding +1, kernel-checked).

rungs.title: Rational first Chern classes and Cartier divisor classes are Hodge classes; F¹ is the kernel of the projection to 𝒪
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-24. Ω⁰ ≅ 𝒪; the stupid truncation 0 → F¹Ω^• → Ω^• → 𝒪[0] → 0 is short exact, so F¹ H^n_dR is exactly the kernel of H^n_dR → ℍ^n(𝒪[0]) (both inclusions); conjugation fixes de Rham images of rational classes. Hence the rational image of an integral degree-two class is a Hodge class iff it vanishes in H²(𝒪); first Chern classes do (exponential sequence), and so do classes of divisors of Cartier data (divisor–Chern, sign +). This is the known half in codimension one for Cartier divisors.

rungs.title: Unique factorization descends along faithfully flat local homomorphisms from a Noetherian local domain to a local UFD
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25 (Mori's descent, local case). Height-one prime P, 0 ≠ a ∈ P: the double colon (aA : (aA : P)) extends to a principal ideal of B (flat base change of colons by the equational criterion; double colons are principal in a UFD), descends to tA (faithful flatness), and equals P (P is associated to A/aA; Nakayama). Mathlib candidate.

rungs.title: The ideal sheaf of a prime divisor is an invertible sheaf represented by Cartier data whose divisor is minus the prime divisor
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. On a smooth projective integral complex scheme, the vanishing ideal sheaf of every prime divisor D = closure {ξ} is invertible (Tau Ceti IsInvertible) and is represented by Cartier data with divisor −D. Route: the vanishing ideal sheaf as S.Modules (HodgeLadder.Divisor.IdealSheaf); near each closed point of D a local equation π (height-one prime of the UFD local ring, principal after inverting one element on an affine open: HeightOneGenerator, LocalGenerator), and 1 away from D; local generation gives generating sections (generates_of_dividesVanishingAt) and hence invertibility (Tau Ceti ofClosedPoints); ord π = 1 at ξ and 0 at other codimension-one points (Mathlib's Scheme.ord), so the Cartier data with local equations π⁻¹ have divisor −D. Sign: the ideal sheaf is 𝒪(−D), so the divisor is −D; −[D] Hodge gives [D] Hodge.

rungs.title: Every invertible sheaf has a unit extension E with L^an ≅ E.sectionSheafOfModules
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. For invertible L on a smooth projective integral complex scheme, L^an is invertible (coherent by Oka, stalks free of rank one, X(ℂ) T1 hence Jacobson; Tau Ceti's closed-point criterion), so it has holomorphic frames σᵢ with σᵢ = gᵢⱼ • σⱼ. The middle sheaf N has sections (n, v) with n locally constant and g(b·)ᵢ·^n · v holomorphic on each Uᵢ (a local predicate); 0 → 𝒪ˣ → N → ℤ → 0 is short exact, with ℤ identified with locally constant functions (constIsoLC). E's chosen lifts of 1 have degree one and transitionUnit y x = vʸ/vˣ; the frames wˣᵢ • σᵢ (wˣᵢ = g(b·)ᵢ · vˣ) on the cover Oₓ ⊓ Uᵢ have E's transitions, and Frames.isoOfSameTransitions gives L^an ≅ E.section. This route does not use the stack's AnalytificationGenerates. Convention: docs/conventions.md, row 'Unit extension of a line bundle'.

rungs.title: Assembly: every prime divisor class is a Hodge class (CycleClassesAreHodgeOne)
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. For a prime divisor D = closure {ξ}: the ideal sheaf is invertible with Cartier data of divisor −D (prime-divisor-ideal-sheaf), its analytification is E.section for a unit extension E (unit-extension-of-invertible), so sheafCycleClassOnCycles 1 (single ξ (−1)) = −[D] is Hodge (chern-classes-are-hodge) and [D] is Hodge. The classes of prime divisors span algebraicCycleClassSpan X 1 (sSup of spans).

rungs.title: Prove the known half: theorem : HodgeLadder.CycleClassesAreHodge
rungs.note: The known half of the conjecture. With it, the upstream HodgeConjecture is equivalent to the equality Hdg^p = span, and the statement cannot hold for a degenerate reason (span accidentally everything). Classical route: a Hodge-cohomology cycle class (El Zein; Voisin2002 ch. 11) comparing cohomology with support in Z of the truncated de Rham complex with the topological class. Large; p = 1 comes first through lefschetz-1-1-equality.

rungs.title: Integral Lefschetz (1,1): the image of c₁ : Pic(X) → H²(X(ℂ); ℤ) equals the integral classes whose rational image is a Hodge class
rungs.note: The literature's form of the theorem (Lefschetz1924, GriffithsHarris1978). Upstream's proof deliberately stops at the rational span. Both inclusions are needed; torsion classes are in the image because they lie in the kernel of H²(ℤ) → H²(𝒪). Integral HC fails in higher codimension (problem.md §2), so this is the one codimension where the integral equality holds.

rungs.title: Computed test case: for projective space ℙ^n over ℂ (n ≥ 1), Hdg^1 = algebraicCycleClassSpan 1, and both are one-dimensional over ℚ
rungs.note: Pins the definitions from both sides at once: a nonzero class in degree 2, a nonzero hyperplane class, and no room for a degenerate reading. Inventory 2026-11-25 (docs/sketches/projective-space-test.md): nothing at the pin computes H² of a positive-dimensional X, and Mathlib has no smoothness or integrality of Proj. Split into sub-rungs on ℙ¹: projective-line-witness, projective-line-point, forget-support-exact (checked), contractible-open-acyclic, projective-line-class-nonzero, projective-line-h2, projective-line-test. This rung keeps the ℙⁿ statement (n ≥ 1); the ℙ¹ case is posted separately as projective-line-test. The hyperplane-class sign is a conventions-register row.

rungs.title: Computed test case on ℙ¹: Hdg^1(ℙ¹; ℚ) = algebraicCycleClassSpan ℙ¹ 1, and both are one-dimensional over ℚ

Routes: integralToRational_mem_hodgeClasses_iff with H²(ℙ¹(ℂ), 𝒪) = 0 and the point class as the rational image of an integral class; or the Cartier route (sheafCycleClassOnCycles_divisor_mem_hodgeClasses) for the divisor of x₀ in Γ(𝒪(1)), which needs a unit extension for 𝒪(1) (part (b) of prime-divisors-cartier) and multiplicity one.

rungs.title: The Clifford algebra of the split form on H ⊕ H^∨ acts on the exterior algebra ∧*H as its spin module, compatible with parity
rungs.note: Research note 2026-11-24 §1. For a torus A with H = H¹(A, ℚ), H*(A, ℚ) = ∧*H, so Spin(H ⊕ H^∨) acts on all of H*(A, ℚ) (Chevalley1954, Mukai1981); Markman's Weil-class construction uses this action through Orlov's equivalence. Pure linear algebra over Mathlib's CliffordAlgebra and ExteriorAlgebra; a Mathlib upstream candidate. Sequenced after the Lefschetz checkpoint.
